_about: Changes newer than visa.json, applied on top of it. Each rule matches a destination and a list of passports. Keep sources so the next person can check them.

rules.summary: South Africa's Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) replaces the e-visa for short visits. Apply online before you fly; approval usually comes within 24 to 72 hours.
notes: The fee is R500 (about US$30). Other visa fees may apply depending on your nationality.
Stays of up to 90 days for tourism or business. You can ask Home Affairs to extend by up to 90 more days.
South Africa's old e-visa closes on 1 December 2026, so apply through the ETA.
At launch, ETA entries were only valid through OR Tambo (Johannesburg), Cape Town International and Lanseria airports. Check this when you apply.
checklist: Apply for your South Africa ETA at eta.dha.gov.za (R500 fee)
Apply at least a week before you fly, in case Home Affairs asks for more documents
Save your ETA approval on your phone and print a copy
Fly into OR Tambo, Cape Town International or Lanseria, unless your ETA says otherwise
Plan to stay no more than 90 days

notes: You can also apply for South Africa's optional Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) at eta.dha.gov.za, which can speed up arrival. It is not required for your passport.
South Africa's e-visa closes on 1 December 2026. Check with the South African embassy whether you can apply through the new ETA or need a visa from the embassy.
